observation: Rebuilding this emblem from shapes and typed text stalled around 40/100 in the early tries, while tracing the redraw with lifted text reached 97.6/100 with every word still live and audited. Two rough edges: poster_fit copies the reference's flaws (the reference's English ran past the end of its bar), and setting the English cleanly inside its bars took a script outside funkbox (find the straight run of the bar, size the text down until it fits with a margin, centre it); the first fit used a regular italic that came out small, a condensed italic filled the bars about 40% better.
suggestion: Give text layers a 'fit_inside' option: a region of the artwork (a colour plus a point, or a traced shape) the words must stay inside with a margin, sized to the largest that fits and centred along it, with condensed faces tried when one is allowed; poster_fit could then respect it instead of chasing a flawed reference.
would_enable: A one-call recreate of any badge or logo with its words as live text, in about a minute instead of two.

observation: Creator guides for local AI video this season put the entry ticket at a 24 GB card for lighter or offloaded setups and 48 GB+ for 14B-class models, so many creators assume local video is out of reach without a big GPU. funkbox already renders without one, but on a fresh headless Linux box (today's cloud run) it first failed with 'could not create an OpenGL 3.3 context; egl: libEGL.so not loaded' and only worked after installing libegl1, libegl-mesa0 and libgl1-mesa-dri by hand; nothing in the error said which packages to install.
suggestion: Add `python -m funkbox doctor`: probe the GL backends (native, EGL, software llvmpipe), and when EGL is missing print the exact install command for the detected distro (apt/dnf/pacman) and set FUNK_GL_BACKEND automatically when only software GL works. Have render and the MCP server show the same hint instead of the bare GLUnavailable error, and report the backend in M-machine-style one-liners.
would_enable: A how-to promo: 'from a bare cloud VM to a rendered Short in 3 commands, no GPU' with the doctor output on a code card and a measured end-to-end time.

observation: The animated-machine genre (Claude building working engines, escapements and differentials as code; CellCog 2026-10-12, Stork.AI 2026-10-23) lives or dies on the mechanism being right: teeth that actually mesh and parts that move in step. Making today's gear train in funkbox meant hand-deriving pitch radii, centre distances and each gear's mesh phase so the teeth interleave, and picking tooth counts so every gear makes a whole number of turns per loop; nothing in funkbox helps with either, and a wrong phase only shows up when you look at frames.
suggestion: Add a small mechanism library to the shader prelude: gear(p, centre, teeth, angle) as an SDF with a shared module, meshWith(gearA, direction, teeth) that returns the meshed gear's centre and phase, and crank/slider helpers. Have loop_write_shader report each gear's turns per loop and warn when one is not a whole number (the loop would jump). Ship one example (examples/gear_train.frag) and a 'machine' preset.
would_enable: A how-to promo: 'a clock escapement or a 4-gear train in 10 lines of GLSL', with the loop check naming the turns per loop on a code card, and a series of mechanism loops (escapement, Geneva drive, planetary gears).

observation: Ad-format guidance this season asks for the same ad in several shapes: Google Ads recommends uploading 16:9, 9:16 and 1:1 versions, and vendor guides map 4:5/1:1 to feeds and 9:16 to Reels. funkbox already renders every shape from one reel, but making today's promo showed the gap after rendering: to show or ship the set I had to run `reel render --format` once per shape (three runs, about 45-70 s each on a 4-core CPU), then hand-build a contact sheet with ffmpeg to check each shape's captions, and nothing tells you which format a caption box crowds once the frame changes shape.
suggestion: Add `reel render --all-formats --sheet`: render every declared format in one call and write formats.png, a side-by-side sheet of each format at the same 3-4 timestamps, plus a per-format line in the text audit (strings checked, exact) so one audit covers the whole set. Have `validate` report, per format, any caption whose box covers more than a set share of the subject or another caption.
would_enable: A behind-the-scenes promo with measured numbers for the whole set: 'four shapes of one ad, rendered in N seconds, every caption audited in every shape', with the formats sheet as the hero shot.

observation: Ad-testing guides this year keep telling creators to ship many variants of one ad, each with a different first scene or hook, and to change one variable per batch (influee's 'Doubling ROAS by Creating Variations of the Same Ad', videotok's creative-testing workflow, segwise on AI UGC testing). In funkbox today each variant means hand-copying the reel.json and copy.json and rendering them one by one.
suggestion: Add `funkbox reel variants <reel> --swap shots[0]=a.json,b.json,c.json` (and an MCP tool reel_variants): one shot list, N alternatives for a named shot or copy id, rendered as N files named by variant, each with its own text audit, plus a contact sheet (the new grid shot can build it) of the first second of every variant so a person can pick before uploading.
would_enable: A how-to promo: 'Five hooks, one shot list': five openings of the demo ad rendered in one command and shown as a grid, each text-audited.

observation: Creators keep losing generations to garbled on-screen text in AI video: Adobe Community threads describe clips that misspell a name or word ('doesn't' three times, 'Housston') and hundreds to ~2,000 credits spent regenerating; guides (CoreReflex, gptproto) say the fix is to keep text out of the generation and add it in an editor afterward. funkbox already adds exact, audited captions on top, but it cannot remove the wrong text a model already baked into a clip.
suggestion: Bring image_trace's lift_text idea to video: a reel source option such as {"video": "clip.mp4", "cover_text": {"rect": [x,y,w,h], "copy_id": "sign"}} that tracks a rectangle across the clip (or takes keyed rects), covers the baked-in text with a blurred or colour-matched patch, and sets the approved line in its place as live text that follows the rect, so the text audit covers it like any caption.
would_enable: A before/after promo: a generated clip with a misspelled sign, fixed in one shot-list line, with the audit proving the new sign exact.

observation: Word-by-word 'karaoke' captions with the current word highlighted are described across 2026 short-form caption guides as the default Shorts/Reels/TikTok style, and the tools that make them time each word from Whisper word timestamps (spoken audio). funkbox's new pill is timed from a characters-per-second estimate (docs/reel.md: 'The voice path has no per-word timings yet, so on voiced shots the pill can drift from the spoken word'), and a style cannot pick WHICH words to emphasise; guides and builders recommend highlighting only key words (about 15-20%), e.g. numbers and punchlines.
suggestion: Two steps for the word highlight: (1) take per-word timings from the local voiceover (Piper can emit phoneme durations; or a local forced-alignment pass) so the pill lands on the spoken word on voiced shots; (2) let the copy deck mark emphasis words (e.g. a 'stress' list per copy line, or *word* markup that the audit strips) so the pill or a colour change hits only those, with the text audit still checking the plain text.
would_enable: A voiced explainer Short where the pill lands on each spoken word and only the key numbers light up, with the audit still proving the words are the approved copy.

observation: Chrome / liquid-metal motion is one of the most-cited 2026 motion looks: trend roundups name metal shaders for logo reveals and chrome motion loops for ads, and open-source front-end libraries now ship 'liquid metal' WebGL shaders (fBm domain warp with fake reflective normals, chrome/gold/mercury palettes). Designers pair it with soft palettes rather than cyberpunk. funkbox's 8 loop looks have no metallic one, so a creator who wants this look has to ask Claude for a new shader each time (as the 11-03 gear-train run did).
suggestion: Add a 'liquid-metal' loop preset (shaders/ + the preset list): domain-warped fBm height field, normals from its gradient, an environment-gradient reflection with palette knobs (chrome, gold, mercury, iridescent) and a soft-pastel background option; keep it periodic in time so `funkbox loop check` passes. Bonus: let a poster/emblem mask (image_trace output or text) be filled with it, for chrome logo reveals.
would_enable: A trend-reaction or feature-spotlight Short: 'chrome logo reveal, rendered on a CPU' - the funkbox emblem traced (F24) and filled with a seamless liquid-chrome loop, checked by machine (F6).

observation: The liquid-metal genre is mostly about LOGOS, not backgrounds: the kits shipping it this autumn take a logo and fill it with chrome (a logo-to-reels kit updated 2026-11-09 renders a 'chrome reveal' reel from a logo; a WebGL2 component updated 2026-10-25 has a text-clipped mode that fills type with the metal). funkbox's new liquid-metal look (shipped from the 11-09 feedback) only renders full-frame: making today's Short, there was no way to put the funkbox wordmark or a traced emblem INSIDE the metal, so the video shows the material but not the use people actually make of it.
suggestion: Add a mask layer to loop recipes: {"type": "mask", "path": "logo.png" | "svg": "emblem.svg" | "text": "FUNK", "font": "Rubik:800"} that clips the layers below it to the shape (alpha from a PNG, an image_trace SVG, or text through the poster text engine so the text audit can still check it), plus an optional bevel (edge normals from the mask's distance field feed metal.frag's lighting so the logo reads as embossed). Ship one example: the funkbox emblem in liquid chrome, loop-checked.
would_enable: A how-to Short: 'your logo in liquid chrome in 3 steps' (image_trace the logo, add one mask line to the recipe, render), ending on a seamless chrome logo loop with the text audit passing on its lettering.

observation: Creators keep being told to keep words out of the video model: a 2026-10-16 HackerNoon guide by a studio founder says readable text in AI video should almost never come from the video model and should be composited as its own layer, while a 2026 motion-trends roundup calls kinetic typography (text that IS the animation) the most-cited motion trend, because short-form is mostly watched muted. funkbox's new typed-text mask makes exactly that kind of shot, but only inside a loop recipe: making today's promo, the word inside the loop could not come from the reel's approved copy deck, so the copy lock and the reel's text audit do not cover it.
suggestion: Let a reel shot fill a copy line with a loop: a shot source like {"loop": "<recipe or preset>", "mask_copy_id": "hook"} that renders the shader inside the approved, hash-locked copy line (same font pipeline as the text mask), and lists that string in final.text_audit.json like any caption. Optionally a per-word reveal so the filled word can type on to the beat.
would_enable: A kinetic-type promo whose headline word is itself the moving loop, rendered from the approved copy and proven exact by the text audit, plus brand-word intros for product ads made from the same edit.

observation: A crowd of new open-source Claude Code skills make video from code (Remotion skills, HeyGen's HyperFrames, claude-motion-design, Charlie Hills' motion-graphics pack; one awesome-list counts 180 such repos). The jobs they advertise are launch clips, kinetic type and especially animated charts and data reels: numbers that count up, bars that grow. funkbox's reel has captions, stills, clips and loops, but no shot that animates a number or a chart, so a 'growth/benchmark' promo is out of reach.
suggestion: Add a 'chart' shot source to the reel: a small CSV or inline list (label, value) drawn as bars or a count-up number, animated over the shot's beats, with the values written into the text audit next to the captions (every number on screen proven equal to the data file). One new source type plus audit entries; reuses the existing caption fonts and brand colours.
would_enable: A behind-the-scenes Short where the render time, test count and tool count grow on screen as an audited chart (every number traced to measured.json), instead of a caption saying it.

observation: This month's 'make videos with Claude' guides (Clippie 2026-11-04, JSON2Video 2026-10-18, CraftStory 2026-10-27) all describe the same loop: describe the video in chat, the tool renders it, then ask for targeted changes. Iterating in chat only works if Claude can see what moved. In today's real loop_render MCP call, the result was the text summary plus one still (the loop's PNG poster frame), so Claude judges a 4-second moving loop from a single frame.
suggestion: Make loop_render (and reel_render) return a filmstrip as the image block instead of the single poster frame: 6 frames evenly spaced across one cycle in a 3x2 sheet, downscaled to about 900 px, built from frames the render already produced. Claude can then see motion, speed and the seam in the chat and propose the next edit.
would_enable: A how-to Short that is one chat screen: the prompt, the loop_render call and a filmstrip of the loop appearing in the conversation, then one follow-up edit.

observation: Creators making Black Friday sale kits this month produce one sale in many shapes and languages: Segmind's 11 Nov test made a homepage hero, an Instagram Story, an email header, a deal card and translated versions, and the translated Spanish line ('DESCUENTO') ran into the product on two of three models. Miraflow's 17 Oct guide lists the same spread (banners, Stories, email headers, thumbnails) for small sellers. funkbox already keeps every string exact (text audit) and resizes a poster to other canvases (stills/resize.py), but a copy deck is one language, and nothing flags a text layer that, after shrinking or resizing, overlaps another layer or the product.
suggestion: Add a layout check to poster render and poster resize: after drawing, compare each text layer's drawn box (already in the text audit) with the other text, shape and product layers and the canvas edges, and fail or warn with the layer ids when they overlap. Pair it with per-language copy decks ("copy": {"en": "sale.copy.json", "es": "sale.es.copy.json"} and --lang), so one poster renders a localized set in every size, each string audited and each layout checked.
would_enable: A promo showing one sale poster rendered in English, Spanish and Hebrew across Story, square and banner sizes, with the layout check catching a long translated line before it hits the product.

observation: Musicians making the short vertical loop that plays behind a track want it to react to their music: the Oct 26 Hypebot round-up of nine tools for this job points them to audio-reactive makers where you upload the song and pick a 3-8 second section, and the canvas guides (Suno.bi, ClipMix) warn that the jump from last frame to first must be invisible. funkbox can do one or the other, not both: a loop with settings.audio is audio-reactive, but its loop check is skipped, and since 2026-11-14 the sidecar even says so ({"status": "skipped", "reason": "audio"}), because a cut of the music is not seamless unless the music is.
suggestion: Add an audio-loop mode to loop render / loop_render: given a track and a start time, detect the beat grid (the reel engine already detects one from music), snap the loop length to a whole number of bars inside 3-8 s, cut that section, crossfade its last 50-100 ms into its start so the audio wraps, and drive iAudio from that wrapped section. Then the picture is a function of a periodic signal and the existing loop check can run again (loop_check status ok instead of skipped).
would_enable: A use-case Short where the loop pulses to a real 2-bar section of a track and the sidecar card shows loop_check status ok with the audio on: an audio-reactive loop that is still machine-checked seamless.

observation: Beat-sync music video tools are pitched hard at Short creators right now: Freebeat's Shorts pages sell a song turned into a 9:16 video with cuts and camera moves synced to the beat, plus animated lyrics; BeatSync PRO runs one landing page per genre (lo-fi, trap, house, hyperpop) for the same promise. The pitch is 'synced', but none of them shows proof of how close the cuts land. funkbox already measures it: today's reel storyboard printed every cut's distance from the nearest beat (3 to 15 ms), but that number disappears after the run.
suggestion: Add a beat audit next to the text audit: when snap_cuts_to_beats is on, the render writes final.beat_audit.json with the detected BPM, each cut's time and its offset from the nearest beat, and ok=false if any cut is off by more than a threshold (say 30 ms). Have promo/measure.py expose it as an M-beats fact so a post can say 'every cut within N ms of a beat' and the reviewer can check it.
would_enable: A behind-the-scenes or myth-vs-fact Short whose claim is a measured number: 'nine cuts, every one within 15 ms of the beat', checked by machine like the text audit.

observation: AI music-visualizer tools sell motion that follows the beat and the song's structure, not just loudness: Freebeat describes BPM-aware analysis that keeps motion on beats and drops and plans loops so the end flows back to the start (Spotify Canvas use), and Neural Frames cites 8-stem analysis. funkbox's new audio loop gives a shader only iAudio (bass, mid, treble, level per frame), so a shader can swell with the bass but cannot flash exactly on beat 1 of a bar, even though the audio-loop cutter already detects the beats and bars.
suggestion: Expose the beat grid the audio-loop cutter already computes as a uniform, e.g. iBeat = (beat phase 0..1, bar phase 0..1, beat index, onset strength), filled for audio loops (and reels' detected grid). Because an audio loop is a whole number of bars, beat and bar phase are loop-safe by construction; add one preset look that uses it and a line in the loop check report.
would_enable: A promo where a shader strobes exactly on every downbeat of a song and still passes the seam check, with the beat audit's numbers on screen as proof.

observation: This week's image-model news puts transparent output up front: ByteDance Seed's Seedream 5.5 (Nov 9) ships transparent RGBA output, and Oakgen's week-of-Nov-9 roundup notes it lets creators skip a separate background-removal step. Ad makers keep compositing generated subjects over other footage (product B-roll, stickers, overlays), and a cut-out is the step between a generated picture and that composite.
suggestion: Add a transparent option to image_generate (MCP) and funkbox image generate --transparent (CLI): after FastSD draws the picture, run the existing remove_background cut-out on it and save an RGBA PNG next to the original, reporting the cut-out's quality score (and the GIMP advice when it is poor), so one call goes from a description to a layer that reel product shots, posters and loops can use.
would_enable: A promo where one sentence becomes a cut-out subject dropped onto a fresh shader loop, all in one MCP call plus a render.

observation: Ad makers now ship every creative in several aspect ratios (9:16 for Reels/Shorts, 4:5 and 1:1 for feeds, 16:9), and the 2026 resize guides all warn about the same failure: a plain crop moves or cuts the subject, logo or call to action, and the big jumps (1:1 to 9:16) need manual checking per size (Pencil's Auto-Resize docs, Segwise's resize guide, Ads Uploader's aspect-ratio docs). funkbox renders all four from one edit, but its storyboard shows one format at a time, so checking every size before a render means one storyboard call and one image per format; making today's promo, I had to render all four just to see them side by side.
suggestion: `funkbox reel storyboard --format all` (and reel_storyboard format="all"): one contact sheet with a row per declared format (each shot's midpoint frame at that size, labelled with the format), so a crop that cuts the subject or a caption that lands badly in one size is caught in one look before rendering.
would_enable: A tip or behind-the-scenes promo that shows the one-look check: a four-row storyboard sheet catching a crop that cuts the subject in 16:9, fixed with a per-format focus line.

observation: People making circular badge and patch logos with AI keep hitting the same two problems: the lettering around the ring (a 2026 hands-on test of five logo tools on a circular 'Bluebird Bakery' badge found only one got the text right every time; an Adobe community bug thread reports generated text coming out skewed and misspelled), and placing ring text by hand. funkbox already gets the letters exact, but making today's patch still took hand arithmetic: each arched line needs its arc radius, x, y and max_width worked out from the circle so it sits centred on the ring, and scaling the badge meant recomputing all of them (and the readability floor then refused the smaller line until min_text was lowered).
suggestion: Add a `ring` placement to poster text layers: {"cx", "cy", "r" (canvas widths), "side": "top" | "bottom"}. funkbox sets the arc (a frown on top, a smile below), centres the line on the circle at that side and caps its width to the ring, so a round badge is a circle shape plus two text layers with the same cx/cy/r. Validation, the text audit entry (geometry records the ring) and docs/stills.md cover it.
would_enable: A how-to: 'A round badge in 3 lines': one circle, two ring lines (top and bottom), render; or a use-case that resizes one badge and its ring text follows.

observation: Faceless-Shorts workflows in 2026 are built around an AI voiceover read from a script, with captions synced to the narration (Creatomate's n8n template, updated 1 Oct 2026, transcribes the generated voiceover to make its subtitles; the Metricool and Pictory faceless-channel guides list voiceover then captions as the core steps). Burned-in captions are only half of it: platforms also take an uploaded caption file (YouTube accepts SRT and WebVTT), which makes the words searchable and accessible and lets viewers turn them off. funkbox already knows every caption's exact text and its first and last frame (the text audit), and every spoken line, but a reel render writes no caption file, so a creator has to retype or re-transcribe words funkbox already has exactly.
suggestion: Have `funkbox reel render` also write `<output>.srt` next to the video: one cue per caption entry in the text audit (start and end from its first and last frame, the exact approved text), so the uploaded captions match the burned-in ones byte for byte. Unit test on a small reel and a docs line in docs/reel.md.
would_enable: A tip: 'Captions twice, same words': the burned-in caption and the uploaded .srt, both from the approved deck, shown side by side.
